name: Extract PDF invoices from Gmail to Google Sheets with OpenAI

parameters.content:
## Extract PDF invoices from Gmail to Google Sheets with OpenAI

### How it works

This workflow monitors a Gmail inbox for PDF invoices, extracts the text from each attachment, and sends the text to an OpenAI-powered information extractor. The extracted invoice fields are then appended as a new row in a Google Sheets ledger.

### Setup steps

- Connect the Gmail credential and configure the trigger to watch the correct inbox, label, or search query for invoice emails with PDF attachments.
- Configure the PDF extraction node to read the expected attachment/binary property from Gmail.
- Connect the OpenAI credential and verify the information extractor schema matches the invoice fields you want to capture.
- Connect the Google Sheets credential and select the target spreadsheet, sheet, and column mappings for the ledger.

### Customization

Adjust the Gmail search filters, the invoice field schema, and the Google Sheets column mapping to match your invoice format and accounting ledger.

## Receive and read invoices

Watches Gmail for incoming invoice emails with PDF attachments and extracts the text content from each PDF for downstream processing. These two nodes form the left-side intake cluster.

## Extract invoice fields

Uses the information extractor with an attached OpenAI chat model to turn the PDF text into structured invoice fields such as vendor, date, total, and invoice number. This is the central AI-processing cluster.

## Append ledger row

Writes the structured invoice data into a Google Sheets ledger as the final output step on the right side of the canvas.

options.systemPromptTemplate: You are an expert accounts-payable clerk. Extract the requested fields from the invoice text precisely. Never invent values: if a field is genuinely absent, return an empty string (or 0 for numbers). Amounts must be plain numbers without currency symbols or thousands separators.

attributes.name: vendor
attributes.description: Name of the company that issued the invoice (the seller / supplier), exactly as printed

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: Invoice number or reference ID exactly as printed

attributes.name: invoice_date
attributes.description: Date the invoice was issued, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: Payment due date formatted as YYYY-MM-DD; empty string if not present

attributes.name: net_amount
attributes.description: Net amount before tax; if only a total is printed, leave 0

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: Total tax / VAT amount; 0 if not present

attributes.name: total_amount
attributes.description: Final total amount payable including tax

attributes.name: currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. USD, EUR, GBP. Infer from the currency symbol if needed

parameters.content:
### 📋 Sheet columns (tab `Invoices`)

ReceivedDate | FromEmail | Vendor | InvoiceNumber | InvoiceDate | DueDate | Net | Tax | Total | Currency | FileName

One row per parsed PDF.

### 🚀 Need more?

I build extended versions of this pipeline: **scanned-PDF OCR**, pushing rows into **QuickBooks/Xero** instead of Sheets, duplicate detection, multi-currency normalization, approval step in Slack/Telegram before posting.

Async delivery, no calls — contact links in my creator profile.
